label: input w at original positions 2-4
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter w during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at early positions. At positions 2, 3 and 4 it fires on every w (precision 1.0) and holds about 99% of the activation mass, with activations near max (about 1.1-1.6). At position 1 it fires weakly on about 40% of w inputs (1.2% of mass). It never fires at position 0 or at position 5 and later. Magnitude is lower when the w repeats an earlier w (in_first=0). It is essentially silent on the delimiter and in the copy phase: only 58 tiny activations, when w is echoed back at step 5 of L=3 sequences. Other tokens never activate it, and the preceding tokens or first token make almost no difference.

issues: Main predicate checks out on test: precision 1.0, recall 0.856, F1 0.923, mass recall 0.987. Running misses on the test split gives 0 false positives. All 7836 missed steps are weak activations (about 0.03-0.08 of max) on w at t=1, which the explanation already describes.
The t=1 claim checks out: w at t=1 scores precision 0.46 and mass 1.2%. The t=1..4 predicate scores test F1 0.924 (precision 0.86, mass recall 0.9999), essentially tied with the chosen predicate.

The magnitude claim is slightly overstated. Mass share per active step at t=4 is about 0.45x that at t=2 or t=3 (t=4: 0.159 mass over 13663 actives; t=3: 0.43 over 16317). So t=4 activations sit near half of max, not uniformly 'near max (1.1-1.6)'. The peak is at t=2-3.

The claim that magnitude is lower for repeated w (in_first=0) is weak. With in_first==0 at t=2..4, mass/recall is 0.0885/0.0795 = 1.11, against 1.15 for the full predicate, a marginal difference at most.

The copy-phase claim is roughly right: 57 activations in the copy phase plus 1 at orig position 5, all negligible. w echoed at step 5 of L=3 sequences gives precision 0.12 and mass 0.00015. Wording nit: 'all at step 5 of L=3' is approximately but not exactly correct.
There is no systematic counterexample class: w is the only token that activates the feature, and the feature is silent at t=0 and at t>=5.
